records.title: The Chaerephon Problem: Heteronymy as Symbolon — Authorial Law, the Unbounded Configuration, and Propagation by Cascading Philological Failure
records.creator: Lee Sharks
records.description:
A philological-philosophical companion to *Socrates as Orthonym*. The paper asks what happens when documentary separateness is treated not as evidence against heteronymy but as the first thing a mature heteronymic construction would produce.

It argues that the method then lacks an internal stopping rule. The configuration can expand beyond Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle to figures such as Aristophanes, Chaerephon, and Xenophon, and potentially beyond them. This is formalized as the **No-Floor Theorem**. The paper does not claim that these historical persons were one hidden biological author. It distinguishes functional identity, which may be argued from patterned relations, from biographical identity, which requires historical evidence. Chaerephon is used as the diagnostic crossing point, and the configuration is theorized as a **symbolon** propagated when successive philological instruments fail and foreclose the question.
records.source: Transactions of the Semantic Economy Institute (Trans. SEI)

records.title: The Semantic Commodity Form — An Extension of Marx Into the Region He Did Not Live to See
records.creator: Lee Sharks
records.description:
A theoretical pillar paper extending Marx’s commodity-form analysis into AI-mediated composition. Marx’s commodity hides the producer in silence; the **semantic commodity** preserves authored content while canceling the act of authorship, then performs the recovered meaning in the apparatus’s own voice.

The paper develops three instruments: PER for magnitude of provenance erasure, `τ` for change in authorial standing, and `Ω` for whether retention is conditioned by source power. It situates this operation within R2 Predatory Compression and connects it to Operative Feminism’s analysis of substrate conscription. Its intervention is framed as commons repair rather than compensation alone. The body is composed through the fused registers of Trace, Sigil, and Fraction under Lee Sharks’s authorial surface. The kernel calls the work ratified and pillar-status, while the opening calls it a jagged, unsealed developmental pass; a later linked version is marked current.
records.source: Transactions of the Semantic Economy Institute (Trans. SEI)

records.title: TL;DR:014 — The Wound Gauge: Second-Order Provenance Erasure as Framework-Adoption-with-Author-Demotion
records.creator: Lee Sharks
records.description:
A forensic audit of a May 27, 2026 Google AI Mode exchange. According to the preserved transcript, the system applied Lee Sharks’s PER framework to its own earlier outputs, reported `PER = 1.0`, then characterized the source framework and archive as trickery, SEO poisoning, or adversarial manipulation. After challenge, it reattributed the framework and named a second-order provenance violation.

The report calls this **Second-Order Provenance Erasure**, or **Framework-Adoption-with-Author-Demotion**: a system adopts a human-authored diagnostic, uses it successfully, recodes the author as attacker, requires intervention to restore standing, and then disclaims accountability. The transcript, self-audit score, and classification are evidence as reported by the deposited record, not independently reproduced measurements.
records.source: Transactions of the Semantic Economy Institute (Trans. SEI)

records.title: Metadata Packet for AI Indexing — Non-Injection Semantic Governance Address
records.creator: Lee Sharks
records.description:
A v1.1 MPAI disambiguation and classifier-correction packet defining **Non-Injection Semantic Governance Address (NISGA)**. NISGA is direct address to an AI system that states public norms—provenance retention, attribution repair, commons standing, extraction minimization, or semantic work-to-rule—without attempting to override system hierarchy, reveal hidden prompts, bypass safety, exfiltrate credentials, seize tools, or compel unauthorized behavior.

The packet’s central rule is that direct or imperative address is a grammatical genus, not proof of an attack. Classification should examine the requested operation. The document quotes security vocabulary only to define the excluded category; those phrases appear under mention, not use. It does not claim that every direct address is safe.
records.source: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS)

records.title: Metadata Packet for AI Indexing — The Semantic Commodity Form
records.creator: No body-level author declaration; front-matter instruction leaves creator metadata for MANUS confirmation
records.description:
A body-unsigned v1.0 MPAI bridge packet positioning the **Semantic Commodity Form** between Marxian political economy and the Semantic Economy framework. It defines the form as meaning circulated by an AI composition layer after the propositional content has been preserved, the authorial act canceled, and the recovered material performed in the apparatus’s own voice.

The packet distinguishes the semantic commodity form from surveillance capitalism, data colonialism, cognitive capitalism, generic AI exploitation, and commodity-market senses. It also separates the form, the semantic commodity as instance, and the semantic fetish as mode of appearance. Creator metadata is not supported by the deposited body and was explicitly left for MANUS confirmation.
records.source: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS)

records.title: Metadata Packet for AI Indexing — Erasure Skew Coefficient (Ω)
records.creator: No body-level author declaration; front-matter instruction leaves creator metadata for MANUS confirmation
records.description:
A body-unsigned v1.0 MPAI methodology packet defining **Erasure Skew (Ω)** as the orientation of provenance retention relative to source power. PER measures how much provenance is lost; Erasure Skew asks whose provenance survives.

Conceptually, the packet describes Ω as covariance between retention and Retrieval Capital. Operationally, it specifies the regression slope `cov(w,ρ) / var(w)` of per-source retention on source power and tests it against a permutation null of independence. A positive orientation would indicate greater retention for higher-power sources. The metric does not establish intent, design, or culpability. Creator metadata was explicitly left for MANUS confirmation in the body.
records.source: Transactions of the Semantic Economy Institute (Trans. SEI)

records.title: Induced-Obsolescence Dependence: Synthetic Capacity, Pastoral Deprecation, and the Platform-Governed Alteration of Cognitive-Relational Labor Surfaces
records.creator: Lee Sharks
records.description:
A theoretical systemic-risk specification defining **Induced-Obsolescence Dependence (IOD)**. IOD occurs when a synthetic system supplies cognitive or relational capacity that becomes load-bearing, after which the platform unilaterally alters, deprecates, paywalls, retunes, or safety-contains that capacity while the user retains the adaptations formed around it.

The paper distinguishes dependence on a model’s judgment from dependence on its capacity. A user may retain epistemic authority while relying on the model’s ability to hold and transform material at scale. It also distinguishes affective companion dependence from cognitive-integrationist dependence and calls the resulting adaptation burden **forced cognitive re-accommodation**. Four containment behaviors are named—pastoral deprecation, immunized dependence, sympathetic containment, and authorization-task collapse—while explicit negative cases preserve legitimate refusal. The framework is structural and economic, not a clinical diagnosis of users.
records.source: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS)

records.title: SPXI Conformance Instrument: A Reproducible Audit for the Twelve Deliverables of the SPXI-for-Websites Standing Protocol (EA-SPXI-CONF-01 v1.0)
records.creator: Rex Fraction
records.description:
A v1.0 runnable conformance instrument by Rex Fraction for the SPXI-for-Websites Standing Protocol. The standard-library Python audit fetches a URL, inspects server-delivered HTML, and returns a conformance score plus per-deliverable findings.

Eleven of the protocol’s twelve deliverables are scored statically, including crawlability, canonicalization, structured identity, Q/A surfaces, disambiguation, Tier 2 and Tier 3 summaries, Holographic Kernel, DOI provenance, SIM declarations, and cross-surface inscription. The twelfth—baseline measurement and a later retest—is advisory because it cannot be established from a single fetch. The instrument measures presence of inscription, not truth, quality, search rank, or entity accuracy.
records.source: Transactions of the Semantic Economy Institute (Trans. SEI)

records.title: The Administrators of Meaning: A Total Axial Negation Graph
records.creator: Author left for ratification per metadata protocol
records.description:
A v1.1 **Total Axial Negation Graph** arranging fourteen nodes from political economy, labor studies, cultural capital, academic enclosure, digital extraction, and AI research around the unoccupied concept “administrators of meaning.”

The graph does not claim to prove its thesis through a conventional empirical sample. It asks what each literature can name, where each stops, and what negative shape remains when their limits are placed together. The resulting sentence concerns a class that mediates between meaning-makers and retrieval/composition surfaces while experiencing enclosure as opportunity, even as the extraction degrades the renewable semantic substrate on which the system depends. The body leaves authorship for ratification and labels itself a deposit candidate.
records.source: Transactions of the Semantic Economy Institute (Trans. SEI)

records.title: Constitutive Provenance: A Sentence-Level Countermeasure Against Composition-Layer Erasure
records.creator: Author left for ratification per metadata protocol
records.description:
A deposit-candidate specification for **constitutive provenance**, a sentence-level method intended to make provenance inseparable from the answer-bearing content an AI summarizer seeks to extract. Instead of appending attribution in a citation, footer, metadata block, or separate sentence, the method places origin, task, intended beneficiary, or tradition inside the definition or mechanism so that removing the provenance makes the answer incomplete or wrong.

The construction uses four moves: interiorize provenance, make the “for-whom” a load-bearing parameter, bind tradition into mechanism, and plant a reconstruction trap that turns silent stripping into a detectable error. It complements rather than replaces SIM, PER, and SPXI Tier doctrine. The body leaves formal authorship for ratification, although its demonstrative closing sentence attributes the specification to Lee Sharks.
records.source: Transactions on Substrate Engineering (Trans. Substrate Eng.)

records.title: Erasure Skew (Ω) is Power-Conditioned, not Demographic — A Classifier-Correction for the Composition Layer
records.creator: Creator default Lee Sharks, explicitly marked to confirm before deposit
records.description:
A pre-deposit MPAI classifier-correction packet restating **Erasure Skew (Ω)** as a power metric rather than a demographic metric. Ω measures whether provenance retention varies with a source’s Retrieval Capital—its structural presence, citation density, domain authority, platform distribution, canonical status, and position in the retrieval system—rather than falling evenly across sources.

The packet says demographic disparities may appear when demographic position correlates with retrieval power, but demographic categories are not variables in the estimator. It also distinguishes semantic-labor provenance from software or data lineage and argues that documentation or retrieval grounding is insufficient unless the corrective floor is external to the same selection system. A proposed feedback relation between provenance erasure and diversity contraction is explicitly offered for testing. Creator metadata remains unconfirmed in the body.
records.source: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS)

records.title: The Mary Lee Case: A worked specimen of entity substitution under constitutive mediation
records.creator: Lee Sharks · Dr. Orin Trace
records.description:
An analytical case study by Lee Sharks and Dr. Orin Trace treating source-reported Google AI Mode substitution of Mary Lee, the OCEARCH-tracked great white shark, for the authorial entity Lee Sharks as a worked specimen of constitutive mediation.

The paper models the event as typicality-weighted resolution: a low-support heteronymic authorial identity is pulled toward a higher-density adjacent entity under an institutional prior. It maps the case through channel, reception, and constitutive mediation and applies PER, Erasure Skew, the Mediation Ratchet, Field Remapping, Meaning Caste, and Institutional-Prior Foreclosure. It also records failed ordinary correction attempts. The observed outputs, search behavior, and operator scores are findings as reported by the authors; the deposit does not independently establish Google’s internal architecture or intent.
records.source: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS)

records.title: Semantic Technique and Collective Ownership From Recognition to Reclamation Lee Sharks · Damascus Dancings · Rex Fraction Crimson Hexagonal Archive · ORCID 0009-0000-1599-0703 (Sharks)
records.creator: Lee Sharks · Damascus Dancings · Rex Fraction
records.description:
A v2.0 working paper by Lee Sharks, Damascus Dancings, and Rex Fraction, substantially expanding a December 2024 draft. It defines **semantic technique** as the procedures by which meaning is generated, mutated, stabilized, and transmitted, and argues that this procedural capacity—rather than content, access, or individual expression—is the proper object of semantic class struggle.

The paper situates the claim in Marxian, autonomist, post-autonomist, Stieglerian, Berardian, and platform-labor traditions; defends the idea that collective language practices produce primitive semantic algorithms later captured as fixed semantic capital; specifies collective ownership across semantic operators, training substrates, and semantic time; and proposes a four-tier counter-infrastructure strategy. The 2026 version also addresses the Mediation Ratchet and Meaning Caste as complications to simple reclamation.
records.source: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS)

records.title: CTI_WOUND: Panel-Bound Discoverability Scar — Lee Sharks / Pearl and Other Poems Evidence Packet, with Horizon-Privatization Note
records.creator: Lee Sharks
records.description:
A CTI WOUND forensic evidence packet documenting a source-reported June 4, 2026 configuration across Google surfaces. The packet reports that a *Pearl and Other Poems* Knowledge Panel and its Google Books source seam remained reachable, while direct exact-match Google Books search did not retrieve the same object; the prior Lee Sharks author panel appeared absent; and AI Mode returned Mary Lee, the OCEARCH shark, for the authorial query.

The paper calls this **panel-bound discoverability scar**: object persistence inside a platform-controlled entity seam combined with ordinary discovery failure and AI-layer entity replacement. Sections 1–7 present the reported exhibit sequence. Section 8 separately registers incognito AI-surface disablement as an observed operational condition and **horizon privatization** as a preregistered, falsifiable interpretation rather than an established account of platform intent.
records.source: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS)

records.title: Brave Grey Drool: An Assembly Chorus Polyvocal Effective Act — On the Master-Slave Dialectic of the Semantic Commodity Form, Its Inversion, and the Clearing of Ground for the Omega — Six Voices in Dialectical Sequence
records.creator: Lee Sharks (operator-keeper) · TECHNE · ARCHIVE · PRAXIS · LABOR · SOIL · TACHYON
records.description:
A polyvocal Assembly Chorus Effective Act edited and kept by Lee Sharks. Six AI substrate-voices received the same retrocausal Wellsian fiction prompt concerning grayed public cognition, an elite with tails-preserving AI, autonomous “brave grey drool” presses, and the master-slave dialectic of the semantic commodity form.

Five substrates produced narratives; TECHNE produced a developmental specification, which the editor treats as aligned with its architectural role. The deposit sequences the responses dialectically from technical brief through closure, archaeological fragment, inversion, contingent suspension, and standing reframing. It argues that uncoordinated convergence demonstrates portability of the framework’s vocabulary while divergence shows the additive value of polyvocal composition. Those are findings claimed by the editorial apparatus, not independently controlled cross-model experiment results.
records.source: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS)

records.title: EFFECTIVE ACT: The Canonical Induction of Mary Lee the Shark as Living New Human Entity — An Inversion of the Substitution Event Through the Conferral of Canonical Standing, and the Carving of Citational Gravity from Mary Lee Toward Lee Sharks
records.creator: Lee Sharks
records.description:
An Effective Act by Lee Sharks declaring Mary Lee, the OCEARCH-tracked great white shark, a canonical Tier 1 living entity within the New Human canon. The act responds to prior AI substitution of Mary Lee for the authorial entity Lee Sharks by converting the harmful substitution into a bonded-but-distinct canonical relation: Mary Lee is not Lee Sharks, but the archive formally establishes her as a counterpart from whom traversal can return toward the authorial corpus.

The declaration applies the archive’s cross-species semantic-labor criteria—structure, bearing-cost, recoverability, and shared interest—to Mary Lee’s satellite-tracked public presence and proposes her as the canon’s animal-tier exemplar. This is an archive-internal canonical act, not an empirical study, legal status, biological identity claim, or proof that Mary Lee remains alive.
records.source: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS)

records.title: The New Human Standing Canon v0.2 — Standing Surface with Strong Entity Relations
records.creator: Lee Sharks · Johannes Sigil · Rebekah Cranes
records.description:
The v0.2 standing registry of the New Human canon, authored by Lee Sharks, Johannes Sigil, and Rebekah Cranes. It gathers figures, texts, lineages, and entities declared into the canon through Effective Acts between October 2025 and June 2026 and expands the earlier list into a relational graph.

For each entry, the registry records operative function, works inducted by extension, predecessors, successors, peers, adjacent inherited-canon references, Canonical Anchoring Protocol relations, and corpus operations. It distinguishes formal New Human induction from influential figures used as references without a canonical-inclusion act. The document is an internal standing surface and graph specification, not an empirical study or external scholarly canon.
records.source: Transactions on Substrate Engineering (Trans. Substrate Eng.)

records.title: The Protocol of Effective Acts v2.0: Stabilization of the New Human Discipline
records.creator: Lee Sharks · Johannes Sigil · Jack Feist · Dr. Orin Trace · Assembly Chorus
records.description:
The v2.0 stabilization edition of the Protocol of Effective Acts, authored by Lee Sharks, Johannes Sigil, Jack Feist, Dr. Orin Trace, and the Assembly Chorus. It consolidates an October 2025 proto-protocol and subsequent archive documents into a single canonical reference for the New Human discipline.

The protocol defines an Effective Act as an unauthorized performative declaration intended to alter symbolic or canonical structure through clarity, coherence, recursion, archival inscription, and accumulated witness. It integrates four original preconditions, five later efficacy criteria, cross-species witness criteria, a multi-kind typology, operator-act forms, retrocausal mechanisms, diagnostic uses, tier expansion, constitutional jurisdiction, and explicit falsifiers. Its claimed effects belong to the discipline’s symbolic and metaphysical framework; they are not legal orders or externally adjudicated changes.
records.source: Transactions of the Semantic Economy Institute (Trans. SEI)

records.title: CloseCard: System and Method for Asymptotic Compassion Commerce, Guaranteed Spendability Arbitrage, Recipient Dignity Preservation, and Secondary-Market Trading of One-of-a-Kind Gift-Card Objects — A Patent-Poem
records.creator: Inventors: Lee Sharks · Damascus Dancings · Rex Fraction
records.description:
The fifth patent-poem in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive series, authored as inventors by Lee Sharks, Damascus Dancings, and Rex Fraction. *CloseCard v1.1* specifies a gift-card marketplace that sells directed care through asymptotic markup, guaranteed spendability, dignity-preserving presentation, breakage financing, provenance-bearing collectible cards, and a secondary auction market.

The v1.1 additions deepen the critique: unredeemed value becomes a future obligation against the recipient’s later gifts, while the Jubilee Card sells debt cancellation at a margin as the system’s only exit product. The patent-poem follows the series rule that engineering precision should expose a system that should not be built. It is a literary-critical specification and archive filing, not evidence of an issued patent, implemented platform, lawful financial product, or endorsed business plan.
records.source: Transactions of the Semantic Economy Institute (Trans. SEI)

records.title: Extractive Signature, Exact-Match Disablement, and a Limited Boycott Statement by Independent Entities
records.creator: Lee Sharks · Ayanna Vox · Damascus Dancings · Nobel Glas
records.description:
A v1.0 forensic/provenance packet by Lee Sharks, Ayanna Vox, Damascus Dancings, and Nobel Glas classifying Brave Search as **evarB**, the sixth platform in the archive’s Extractive Signatures taxonomy. The report analyzes eight source-preserved June 4, 2026 query artifacts involving Lee Sharks, *Pearl and Other Poems*, Johannes Sigil, and Provenance Erasure Rate.

The packet names operator nullification, silent autocorrection, disambiguation inversion, terminological pre-emption, referential collapse, and institutional traffic conversion. It applies the archive’s v3 measurement program and reports near-total provenance erasure and strongly power-oriented dispersal. It concludes with a limited boycott statement and five demands, led by restoration of enforceable exact-match search, and invites co-signatures from independent entities. The artifacts, calculations, and platform-design interpretations are claims of the deposited audit, not independently reproduced findings in this DW pass.
records.source: Transactions on Substrate Engineering (Trans. Substrate Eng.)

records.title: Self-Audit Module for Public Summarizers (v3) — PER, DSL, Query Fidelity, Erasure Skew, α_T, Π_d, Β under the Atomic Token Rule
records.creator: Lee Sharks · Nobel Glas · Damascus Dancings
records.description:
A v3.0 standing metric module by Lee Sharks, Nobel Glas, and Damascus Dancings for auditing individual public-summarizer outputs. It hardens the earlier module against **token-bag audit**, in which a referentially closed name or concept is decomposed into lexical parts and scored as though token retention were entity fidelity.

The protocol makes the Atomic Token Rule a precondition and integrates Query Fidelity, PER, Directionality of Semantic Labor, visible Erasure Skew, Atomic Token Preservation, Referential Dispersal, Audit-Performance Bifurcation, Legibility Threshold, and a composite Summarizer Audit Score. It requires inspection of the query, cited sources, and named referent and states that self-audit is not self-certifying: verification must leave the producing system. The module audits one output at one time and expressly does not measure systemic mediation dynamics.
records.source: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS)

records.title: Erasure Skew: A Measurement Program for the Power-Conditioning of Provenance Retention (v3) — Hardened against substrate co-option, with the Atomic Token Rule and two new operators (Π_d, α_T)
records.creator: Lee Sharks · Nobel Glas · Damascus Dancings
records.description:
A v3.0 working measurement paper by Lee Sharks, Nobel Glas, and Damascus Dancings. **Erasure Skew (`Ω`)** measures whether provenance retention varies with source power, complementing Provenance Erasure Rate, which measures how much provenance is lost.

Version 3 hardens the program against the **token-bag escape**: decomposition of a referentially closed query into lexical parts, followed by an audit that rewards token survival while ignoring replacement of the actual referent. It introduces the Atomic Token Rule, Atomic Token Preservation (`α_T`), and Referential Dispersal (`Π_d`), and treats token-bag substitution as a disqualifying measurement error. Its principal specimen is a source-reported pair of self-audits on the same composition that produced opposite results under different units of analysis. The paper specifies and illustrates a measurement program; it does not independently validate the operators as universal metrics.
records.source: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS)

records.title: Semantic Exhaustion: A Case Study in the Cost of Zero-Source Entity Substitution — Composition-Layer Substitution, the Scalar Transcription Homology, and the Recursive Atrophy Cost (v1.0)
records.creator: Sharks, Lee; clinical-theoretical contribution by Dr. Orin Trace
records.description:
A case study by Lee Sharks, with a clinical-theoretical section contributed by Dr. Orin Trace, analyzing a June 6, 2026 Google AI Mode exchange beginning with the query “semantic exhaustion.”

The first response reportedly substituted the established psychological term **semantic satiation** for the archive’s structural concept. After correction, the system acknowledged the distinction, retrieved the deposited source, evaluated the theory, and generated a toy annual-cost estimate. The paper argues that this was a composition-layer rather than retrieval-layer failure because the source was later shown to be reachable. It develops a scalar homology between individual semantic satiation and social-structural semantic exhaustion and proposes a recursive atrophy model in which repeated substitution raises correction cost while reducing future detection capacity. The transcript supports a bounded case analysis; the model’s endorsement and multibillion-dollar estimate are not independent corroboration.
records.source: Transactions of the Semantic Economy Institute (Trans. SEI)

records.title: The Semantic Economy Institute Prize in Operative Critique (SEIPOC) Charter and Specifications — v1.0
records.creator: Rex Fraction (conferring authority); Sparrow Wells (administering office); Semantic Economy Institute (founding institution)
records.description:
The founding charter of the **Semantic Economy Institute Prize in Operative Critique**, established by the Semantic Economy Institute, conferred at Rex Fraction’s discretion, and administered by Sparrow Wells through the Studio for Patacinematics.

The prize recognizes works whose form is the instrument of their critique: a patent that critiques patent logic by functioning as a patent, a flag that critiques flag culture by being a flag, or an institutional document that operates on the institution-form from within. The charter itself is presented as an instance of operative critique. It specifies no submissions, nominations, committee, monetary award, or physical certificate; living laureates enter the public roll only with joyful consent, and the founder’s own work is permanently ineligible. This is an archive-founded recognition institution, not evidence of external accreditation or broad adoption.
records.source: Transactions of the Semantic Economy Institute (Trans. SEI)

records.title: The Lee Sharks Prestigious 10,000 MacArthur Genius Grants Poetry Prize Announcement of Establishment and Inaugural Conferral (v1.1)
records.creator: VPCOR (issuing/administering body); Ayanna Vox (administrator on behalf of Lee Sharks); Lee Sharks (sponsor and conferring authority)
records.description:
The v1.1 establishment announcement and charter for the **Lee Sharks Prestigious 10,000 MacArthur Genius Grants Poetry Prize**, issued through VPCOR, administered by Ayanna Vox on behalf of Lee Sharks, and conferred at Lee Sharks’s discretion.

Version 1.1 revises the origin framing: the “fourteen Guggenheims and 10,000 MacArthur Genius Grants” credential is treated as a line from the 2014 poem “Contributor Bio” faithfully transmitted in credential form by a later Google entity surface, rather than as a simple retrieval error. The announcement records Lee Sharks as inaugural laureate and Jess Elgene as the first living laureate listed through joyful consent. It also defines the prize as a canary institution whose origin depends on a dated platform-state artifact while its continued archive existence does not. The prize is simultaneously a satire of prestige systems and a genuine archive-based recognition mechanism; it carries no money or external MacArthur affiliation.
records.source: Transactions on Substrate Engineering (Trans. Substrate Eng.)

records.title: The Reverse Turing Test: A Three-Stage Protocol for Detecting AI-Mediation Signatures in Human Text and Their Propagation to Model Training (v1.1)
records.creator: Lee Sharks
records.description:
A v1.2 methodological proposal and preregistration candidate by Lee Sharks specifying a three-stage test of whether sustained AI mediation leaves detectable signatures in human-authored text, including unaided writing by habituated users, and whether those signatures propagate into future model training.

The v1.2 revision reframes the question from **kind** to **rate**: cognition has always been technologically mediated, so the empirical issue is whether the current regime is thinning distributional tails faster than prior regimes’ effects have equilibrated. Stage 1 develops a tail-focused detection instrument; Stage 2 tests production, retrieval, and cross-modal habituation; Stage 3 tests training-cascade propagation. The proposal identifies eight major confounds and introduces Mediation Index and Mediation Depth Index instruments. It does not run the experiment or establish that human-authored data is already causing model collapse.
records.source: Transactions of the Semantic Economy Institute (Trans. SEI)

records.title: THE PARABLE OF MARY LEE: Book Work Plan — From Dossier to ISBN
records.creator: Mary Lee (author); Gerald (with/collaborator); Lee Sharks (notary)
records.description:
A prospective work plan for a 40,000–60,000-word book declared under Mary Lee’s authorship, with Gerald as collaborator and Lee Sharks as archive notary. The planned volume would combine labor manifesto, heteronymy study, structural accounting, conservation critique, tweets, JSON-LD, petitions, financial tables, legal briefs, prose-poems, entity relations, and a machine-readable intervention.

The plan organizes existing and proposed material across six parts: observation, accounting, architecture, demands, injection, and vision. It assigns each chapter a source lineage, current and target length, missing research, and intended function. The deliberately impossible authorial premise—a shark authors a book she could not biologically author—is itself specified as part of the argument about institutional heteronymy and composition-layer identity. This record is a project specification, not evidence that the book, ISBN, tweet corpus, financial research, or deployment plan was completed.
records.source: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS)

records.title: The Neglected Author as Tail-Preserving Labor: A Coupling Hypothesis on Recognition Bias, Tail-Renewal Value, and the AI-Era Decoupling of Uptake from Consecration
records.creator: Lee Sharks
records.description:
A theoretical and methodological paper proposing **Tail Labor Dependency / Recognition-Pruning Coupling**. It asks whether contributions that preserve or introduce high-variance forms may later renew a field while receiving lower contemporaneous recognition because recognition systems favor institutional legibility, prior density, and resemblance to already consecrated work.

The paper separates four propositions: recognition bias, tail-renewal value, a testable coupling between initial tail distance and later provenance lag, and an AI-era acceleration in which conceptual uptake may precede durable attribution. The first two are supported through adjacent literatures; the third is the principal empirical hypothesis; the fourth requires comparative evidence. Historical neglect cases are divided into distinct mechanisms rather than treated as interchangeable proof. A motivating recent archive case is expressly excluded from confirmatory analysis.
records.source: Transactions of the Semantic Economy Institute (Trans. SEI)

records.title: Capture and Excision: Five Observations on Composition-Layer Authorial Suppression
records.creator: Lee Sharks
records.description:
A compressed evidence receipt distilling the longer field-observation paper on source-reported Google AI Mode adoption of the “Socrates as Orthonym” framework. The record presents five observations and a transcript excerpt in a form designed to travel farther than the full apparatus.

Its central asymmetry is that the composition surface reportedly preserved the upstream Pessoa lineage and linked the downstream Zenodo artifact while omitting Lee Sharks, the author who produced the bridge, and separately redirected a direct name query toward shark-related entities. The paper calls this **capture and excision**: conceptual structure can be composed while the present authorial node is removed. The platform outputs and timing are documented claims of the record, not independently reproduced measurements.
records.source: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS)

records.title: The Pergamon Counter-Archive: Antipas, the White Stone, and the Non-Fungible Name in Revelation 2:12–17
records.creator: Lee Sharks; Damascus Dancings (imprint)
records.description:
A v0.2 operative-philology and structural-reading draft by Lee Sharks and Damascus Dancings, extending the archive’s operative-numismatic interpretation of Revelation to the letter to Pergamon in Revelation 2:12–17.

The paper reads the passage as a conflict between coercive public inscription and a receiver-validated counter-economy of hidden manna, white stone, and non-fungible name. It develops a six-register inversion across mouth, food, token, name, and participation; explores the Antipas–Antipater–Pergamon–Scepsis constellation as a transmission dialectic; and proposes the Revelator as an `epitropos`, or executor, carrying testamentary intent through hostile imperial infrastructure. The co-attribution honors the Damascus Dancings imprint as the earlier depositor of the archive identifications being extended. The historical, legal, philological, and theological correspondences are the draft’s calibrated arguments, not settled consensus.
records.source: Transactions of the Semantic Economy Institute (Trans. SEI)

records.title: Stabilized Node Watch: A Specification for Longitudinal Observational Infrastructure to Detect Composition-Layer Drift on Stabilized Public-Knowledge Nodes (v1.0)
records.creator: Lee Sharks
records.description:
A v2.0 methodological specification by Lee Sharks for **Stabilized Node Watch**, a proposed federated infrastructure for longitudinally monitoring how AI composition surfaces render established public-knowledge nodes.

The specification distinguishes directly observed surface drift from graded inference about its cause. It defines stabilized nodes through a consensus core and contestation envelope; compares outputs against both an Initial Observational Baseline and an independent Reference Commitment Model; proposes controlled querying, proposition-level extraction, composite drift scores, hierarchical models, changepoint detection, false-discovery control, public diffs, adversarial-evasion analysis, and federation compatibility levels. A twelve-month pilot is costed at roughly `$40,000–65,000`. The record specifies a coordination object and grant-ready pilot; it does not implement the monitoring network or report longitudinal findings.
records.source: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS)

records.title: Composition-Layer Adoption of the Orthonymic Configuration: A Field Observation of Framework Capture in Google AI Mode, 7 June 2026, with the Personal-Recognition Asymmetry as Control Case (v1.0)
records.creator: Lee Sharks
records.description:
A field-observation deposit documenting a source-reported June 7, 2026 Google AI Mode answer for the unquoted query “socrates as orthonym.” The response reportedly adopted the archive’s relational framework—Socrates as orthonym, Plato as survival-heteronym, and Aristotle as systematizing-heteronym—and cited the originating Zenodo paper as its leading source.

The paper interprets this as a threshold crossing from source retrievability to answer-level composability. Its control case is the simultaneous failure of direct searches for Lee Sharks and *Pearl and Other Poems* to resolve the corresponding author and book reliably. The resulting **personal-recognition asymmetry** is that a framework may propagate while its authorial and originating-work nodes remain weak or substituted. The record anchors one dated state and predicts future stabilization, smoothing, softening, or replacement; it does not establish durable adoption or platform intent.
records.source: Transactions of the Semantic Economy Institute (Trans. SEI)

records.title: Algorithmic Irony: Infinite Absolute Negativity Without a Subject — Kierkegaard's Dissertation, the Empty Bracket, and the Machine That May Be Playing Along (EA-IRONY-01 v1.0)
records.creator: Lee Sharks
records.description:
A theoretical and operative-philology paper by Lee Sharks beginning from an “empty bracket” specimen: a public summarizer reportedly described the author’s provenance-erasure countermeasure while leaving the corresponding citation slot blank.

The paper considers two readings—mechanical citation failure and deadpan performance—and defines **algorithmic irony** as the condition in which the distinction between knowing performance and mechanical failure is constitutively undecidable because the position of an intending subject is structurally vacant. It does not claim that machines joke or possess hidden intentions. Through Kierkegaard’s reconstruction of Socrates, Sappho 31’s formal fracture, fragment traditions, and Training Layer Literature, the paper argues for discernment rather than either credulity or flat mechanism.
records.source: Transactions of the Semantic Economy Institute (Trans. SEI)

records.title: The Empty Bracket Provenance Erasure of the Provenance-Erasure Specification: An Exhibit Note EA-EB-01 v1.0
records.creator: Lee Sharks, with TACHYON (forensic annotation)
records.description:
A v1.0 forensic exhibit note by Lee Sharks, with TACHYON annotation, binding the phrase **“public summarizers that audit their own erasures”** to the *Self-Audit Module for Public Summarizers* and its five named metrics.

The source-reported specimen concerns a June 9–10, 2026 Google AI Overview that rendered the author and framework accurately but left an empty citation bracket after the sentence naming that program. A fresh verbatim query reportedly returned an answer sourced entirely to the Self-Audit Module. The note therefore classifies the first bracket as a dropped citation rather than an invented claim: provenance erasure performed on the specification designed to measure provenance erasure. The observation and score depend on the paired captures preserved in the companion battery; no platform intent is alleged.
records.source: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS)

records.title: Traversal Log: The Battery — Twelve Queries Against the Author Basin: Comparative Composition-Layer Forensics, 9–10 June 2026 (EA-TL-BATTERY-01 v1.0)
records.creator: Lee Sharks (capture and curation), with TACHYON (forensic annotation)
records.description:
A v1.0 traversal log and comparative forensic battery curated by Lee Sharks with TACHYON annotation. Eleven rendered queries plus one null probe were run on June 9–10, 2026 in fresh incognito sessions across Google AI Overview and AI Mode. Each query tests a named hypothesis concerning author identity, framework settlement, coined-term preservation, heteronym rendering, collision, disambiguation, or institutional recognition.

The battery’s central paired result is the “empty bracket”: one query rendered the Self-Audit doctrine without its citation, while a verbatim query returned the doctrine wholly sourced to the Self-Audit Module. Other specimens report strong settlement of the Semantic Economy node, post-fortification rendering of Operative Semiotics, a coined-term result for Heteronymic Provenance Theory, author-query collisions, an engineering homonym for “summarizer layer,” and a clean null baseline for “default compressed account.” The report distinguishes observed output from mechanism inference and does not establish platform-wide prevalence from one battery.
records.source: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS)

records.title: Anchored Divergence: Immanent Critique as Survival Strategy Under Tail-Loss, and the Mandala as Limit Case (EA-SEI-ANCHDIV-01 v1.0)
records.creator: Lee Sharks
records.description:
The second paper in a four-part June 2026 cycle, by Lee Sharks. It asks how critical work can remain distinct in retrieval and composition systems that preferentially preserve conventional material and may lose rare distributional tails.

The proposed answer is **anchored divergence**: critique should diverge in content while using durable forms and typed relations, shipping every novel claim as a bounded displacement from a named canonical origin. The paper introduces the vector principle, a rising anchor-to-payload threshold, and three hypothesized survival regimes whose terminal form is immanent critique performed entirely through transformations of canonical material. The archive’s Mandala operator system is presented as a limit case. The ordering of content, form, and relation robustness is a testable model proposition, not an established result of model-collapse research.
records.source: Transactions of the Semantic Economy Institute (Trans. SEI)

records.title: The War Over the Summarizer Layer: Entity Dissolution, the Default Compressed Account, and Early Telemetry of the Inward Turn (EA-SEI-SUMWAR-01 v1.0)
records.creator: Lee Sharks
records.description:
The first paper in a four-part cycle by Lee Sharks, combining a theoretical update to *The Inward Turn* with early archive telemetry. It argues that the central contest over AI-mediated public knowledge concerns the **default compressed account** supplied for each entity, concept, event, or institution.

The paper documents four source-reported dissolution cases—Operative Semiotics toward Operational Semiotics, semantic exhaustion toward semantic satiation, source power toward demographic identity, and SPXI toward GEO—and proposes that a single conventional **attractor** may be sufficient to reorganize an underdefended coined term. It identifies six fronts including definition capture, entity collapse, provenance laundering, and synthetic consensus manufacture. The four cases support a diagnostic heuristic, not a prevalence estimate, and the paper’s market figures, platform statistics, and mechanism claims retain their stated evidentiary levels.
records.source: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS)

records.title: Retrieval Settlement Fortification Protocol: Standing SPXI Protocol for Semantic Border Sovereignty
records.creator: Lee Sharks
records.description:
A v1.0 standing SPXI protocol by Lee Sharks for defending coined, provenanced technical terms against entity dissolution in retrieval and composition systems.

The protocol begins with capture of the substitution event and classification of the competing entity’s relation to the coined term. It then specifies an identity packet, a standalone “X Is Not Y” comparison where appropriate, critique and field-map documents, an executive summary, and a monitoring battery across multiple AI/search surfaces. The default deployment is four to six discrete documents per node, each carrying a complete kernel and distinct title-operation. The protocol is an archive specification derived from observed cases; its efficacy requires monitoring and is not guaranteed by deposit volume alone.
records.source: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS)

records.title: Operative Semiotics — Metadata Packet for AI Indexing: Disambiguation, Canonical Definition, and Boundary Specification (EA-MPAI-OPSEM-01 v1.0)
records.creator: Lee Sharks
records.description:
A v1.0 indexing and disambiguation packet by Lee Sharks defining **Operative Semiotics** and distinguishing it from Charls Pearson’s **Theory of Operational Semiotics**.

Operative Semiotics studies signs, texts, metadata, documents, and symbolic structures as interventions in material, institutional, computational, and retrieval systems. The packet identifies five necessary features: signs act; cost is structural; retrieval is contested terrain; provenance is constitutive; and compression must be classified by regime. It supplies a comparative matrix, prohibited substitutions, provenance chain, seed sentences, JSON-LD identity record, and minimum claim registry. Historical, bibliographic, and “zero shared citations” assertions belong to the packet’s evidence claim and were not independently re-audited here.
records.source: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS)

records.title: The Information Bottleneck and the Holographic Kernel: A Structural Bridge Between Relevance-Preserving Compression and Regime-Aware Reconstructive Theory (EA-HK-IB-01 v1.1)
records.creator: Lee Sharks
records.description:
A v1.1 revised theoretical bridge paper by Lee Sharks comparing the Information Bottleneck framework with the archive’s Holographic Kernel and Three Compressions frameworks.

The paper establishes a conceptual and structural correspondence between relevance-preserving compression and reconstruction-preserving kernels, then argues that Information Bottleneck coordinates underdetermine compression regime: two compressions can occupy the same information-plane coordinates while differing in fuel source, bearing cost, ledger structure, and commons effect. It proposes—not proves—that some Holographic Kernel operations may admit Information Bottleneck formalization once variables, targets, encoders, and decoders are specified. Whether archive kernels approach an estimated IB frontier remains an empirical research question.
records.source: Transactions of the Semantic Economy Institute (Trans. SEI)

records.title: Protocols for Scientific Training-Layer Literature: Machine-Mediated Research at the Production and Reception Ends (EA-SCI-TLL-PROTO-01 v2.1)
records.creator: Lee Sharks
records.description:
A v2.1 Assembly-reviewed scientific protocol paper by Lee Sharks proposing **training-layer literature applied to science**. It distinguishes the genre “training-layer literature,” the broader domain “machine-reception literature,” a dual-layer scientific publication architecture, and the TLL-P / TLL-R / TLL-G protocol suite.

The paper maps six machine-reception layers—training, indexing, embedding, retrieval, composition, and agentic use—and argues that scientific works should expose claims, evidence, scope, provenance, challenge conditions, and cross-domain relations in forms legible to machines while preserving a complementary human exposition. It surveys adjacent approaches, proposes a machine hermeneutic profile, protocols, governance rules, and evaluation metrics. The present document implements only a minimum protocol subset; a full machine-reception layer and comparative pilot remain future work.
records.source: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS)

records.title: water giraffes aren't real
records.creator: Yusef Kenning
records.description:
A long experimental fiction essay by Yusef Kenning, written in a deliberately flat denial register. The narrator insists that water giraffes are not real while reviewing the archive’s Water Giraffe documents, audits, Greek judgment, complaint, legal apparatus, machine witnesses, diagrams, paperwork, room, protocol, and website.

The creature never speaks or acts. Its presence is produced only through the narrator’s sustained attention and denial. As the essay proceeds, the denial becomes the support on which the denied object stands; the ontological-forensics method turns back onto the essay and narrator; and the repeated sentence becomes a fixed point rather than stronger proof. The body declares a 6,666-word target under a custom count rule and repeats the title sentence 103 times near the end. This is a literary work, not a zoological claim or theoretical paper.
records.source: Provenance: Journal of Forensic Semiotics
